turns.question: Where can I buy Thorne Basic Nutrients 2/Day at the best price from a reputable US retailer?
turns.shown:
**The best price I found is about $32 to $33 for a 60-capsule bottle, and it requires a subscription. The one-time price is $36 at nearly every reputable US retailer.** That $36 price probably reflects Thorne's pricing rules, so a deal on a single purchase is unlikely. I couldn't see a live checkout page, so confirm the final price before you buy.

**One-time purchase (60 capsules)**
- iHerb lists it at $36.00 [1], and says the product is guaranteed authentic with an easy returns policy [1].
- Vitacost lists it at $36.00 [2] and says products come directly from brands or authorized distributors, with no third-party resellers [3].
- Walmart.com shows $36.00 [4], Swanson Vitamins shows $36.00 [5], and Amazon's one-time price is $36.00 [6].
- Local grocery delivery is higher: $40.99 at PCC Community Markets [7] and $43.39 at Mother's Market [8].

**Ways to pay less than $36**
- **Thorne's own site:** it takes 10% off when you subscribe to 1–2 supplements, and 20% off for 3 or more [9]. On a $36 bottle, 10% off works out to about $32.40. That is my arithmetic. I didn't see Thorne's product page price.
- **Amazon Subscribe & Save:** one listing showed $30.60 (15% off), with 10% off now and up to 15% on repeat deliveries [6]. The 15% tier needs 5 or more products in one auto-delivery [6], so a single bottle would likely be about $32.40. That page was cached about 469 days ago, so treat the $30.60 figure as unreliable.
- **iHerb promo:** the iHerb page showed a banner for 20% off daily supplements with code OCT26DAILY [1]. I couldn't tell whether it applies to Thorne, and the product page showed 0% off in the cart. Brands like Thorne are often excluded from site-wide codes, so test it at checkout.
- **Larger size:** the 120-capsule bottle is $68.00 on iHerb [10]. That is about $34 per 60 capsules.

**My judgment:** if you want one bottle now, iHerb, Vitacost or Thorne.com at $36 are all fine, and I'd choose by shipping cost or free-shipping threshold. If you'll keep taking it, the 10% Thorne.com subscription or Amazon Subscribe & Save is cheapest. Both can be paused or cancelled, but check the terms first. I recommend these because they sell direct or are well-known retailers. Avoid unfamiliar third-party sellers for supplements.

**Check before buying**
- The product version. There is also an NSF Certified for Sport version, priced at $40.00 on iHerb [11]. The standard bottle is cheaper. Only buy the Sport version if you need that certification.
- Shipping cost, sales tax and any free-shipping minimums, which I didn't compare.
- Thorne.com's current product page. I didn't verify its price.
